purpose: Authentic 1941 German Army Enigma messages with their recovered keys and published raw plaintext. tests/test_historical_messages.py deciphers each with enigma.EnigmaI and requires the published raw plaintext letter for letter, so the machine model is checked against real traffic, not only against keys this repository planted itself.

source.attribution: Olaf Ostwald and Frode Weierud, 'Modern breaking of Enigma ciphertexts', Cryptologia 41(5), 395-421, companion page at CryptoCellar
source.license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, as data/phase5/README.md records for the CryptoCellar material
source.sha256_note: Identical to the copy fetched for data/phase2/held-out-plaintexts.json on 2026-10-06.

conventions.key_as_published: Reflector and wheel order (B423 = UKW B, wheels IV II III left to right), ring settings, start position (message setting), ten plugs.
conventions.discriminant: The first group is the Kenngruppe and is not enciphered; deciphering starts at the second group.
conventions.ciphertext: The groups after the discriminant, whitespace removed.
conventions.raw_plaintext: The page's raw plaintext, whitespace removed; garbles kept as published, X as word separator, Q for CH.

messages.note: The page prints No. 1's key line for this message, start position DEI included, and DEI does not decipher it. Under the published wheels, rings and plugs, ZAQ is the only one of the 17,576 start positions that reproduces the published raw plaintext (24 of 24 letters); the next best agrees on 10. Searched 2026-10-20.
